title: Where per-project CTOC configuration should live
context: CTOC needs a place to store each project's configuration: the enforcement mode, the detected technology stack, and the quality-gate commands. The realistic choice is between a single shared configuration in the user's home directory that governs every project on the machine, and a per-project configuration folder that is committed alongside the repository it governs. The shared location needs no per-repository setup, but it cannot vary from one project to another. The per-project location travels with the code and can differ per repository, at the cost of existing in each repository.
decision: Where should a project's CTOC configuration live?
constraints: Configuration must be able to differ from one project to another; two repositories on the same machine can require different enforcement modes and different detected stacks.
Configuration should be versioned together with the code it governs, so that checking out any past commit also restores the settings that were in force at that commit.
A new contributor who clones the repository should receive the project's settings automatically, without a separate machine-level setup step.
The recommendation is judged on outcome quality, which here means correct isolation between projects and reproducibility from the repository, not on how little initial setup the option requires.
